skill.name: nla-create
skill.description: Create a Natural Language Agreement escrow on-chain with the nla CLI. The skill gathers escrow terms, checks wallet and network prerequisites, crafts an evaluable demand, and runs escrow creation.
skill.summary: Create on-chain Natural Language Agreement escrows with guided nla CLI setup and demand drafting.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: The audit found many Markdown backtick false positives, but several findings are real because the skill runs the nla CLI and handles wallet private keys. The highest risks are private key exposure and on-chain escrow creation that can lock ERC20 tokens. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Private key handling through CLI arguments or environment variables
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a wallet connector, hardware wallet, or encrypted local wallet flow. Do not ask users to paste private keys into chat, shell history, or process arguments.

remediation.issue: Fund-locking on-chain escrow command can run without an explicit final review
remediation.suggestion: Add a mandatory confirmation step that repeats network, token, amount, oracle address, provider, model, and estimated fees before executing nla escrow:create.

remediation.issue: User-controlled demand and prompt text are passed to a shell command
remediation.suggestion: Escape shell arguments carefully or use a safer argument-passing mechanism. Reject values that contain unexpected control characters or unbalanced quotes.

remediation.issue: Local development command starts services and deploys contracts
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before running nla dev and explain that it starts Anvil, deploys contracts, creates tokens, and starts an oracle.

content.value_statement: Creating a token escrow with natural language conditions requires exact parameters and careful wallet setup. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through requirement gathering, demand drafting, checks, and nla CLI execution.
actual_capabilities: Collects required escrow details, including demand, amount, token address, and oracle address.
Checks whether the nla CLI, network, and wallet are ready before escrow creation.
Helps draft clear natural language demands that an AI oracle can evaluate.
Builds an nla escrow:create command with optional provider, model, and arbitration prompt settings.
Explains the escrow UID output and the next steps for fulfillment and collection.
Documents supported networks and local development setup for nla workflows.
limitations: Requires the nla CLI, a funded wallet, and access to a supported EVM network.
Amounts must be entered in the token smallest unit; the skill does not convert decimals.
Demand text, provider, model, and prompt data can become publicly visible on-chain.
AI arbitration quality depends on the configured oracle, model, and available evidence.

use_cases.title: Launch a conditional token bounty
use_cases.description: Create an escrow that releases ERC20 tokens when a submitted fulfillment satisfies a written demand.

use_cases.title: Test NLA workflows on a development network
use_cases.description: Use local or testnet settings to verify networks, wallets, contracts, and oracle behavior before mainnet use.

use_cases.title: Draft clearer oracle arbitration terms
use_cases.description: Turn vague escrow goals into specific demands that are easier for an AI oracle to judge.

prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create an NLA escrow. Ask for each required value, check my setup, and explain every step before running commands.

prompt_templates.prompt: Review this escrow demand for clarity, testability, and public visibility. Suggest a tighter version before I create the escrow.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a testnet escrow
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through creating an NLA escrow on a test network. Confirm the network, token, oracle, wallet, and arbitration model first.

prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create an escrow with a custom arbitration provider, model, and prompt. Validate the placeholders and summarize all public on-chain fields.

output_examples.input: I want to escrow tokens for someone who submits a useful technical report.
output_examples.output: The skill asks for the token, amount, oracle, network, and report acceptance criteria, then rewrites the demand for clearer arbitration.

output_examples.input: Create a Sepolia escrow using Anthropic arbitration.
output_examples.output: The skill checks the active network and wallet, confirms the provider and model, then prepares the escrow creation command for review.

output_examples.input: The command returned an escrow UID.
output_examples.output: The skill highlights the UID, explains why it must be saved, and describes how fulfillment and collection use that identifier.

best_practices: Use testnets or local development before locking valuable tokens on mainnet.
Keep demands specific, verifiable, and free of secrets because terms may be public.
Confirm network, token address, oracle address, amount, and wallet before execution.
anti_patterns: Do not paste private keys into chat or store them in shell history.
Do not create escrows with vague demands that an oracle cannot evaluate.
Do not run mainnet commands until testnet behavior and wallet balances are verified.

faq.question: What is an NLA escrow?
faq.answer: It is an on-chain escrow that locks ERC20 tokens until an AI oracle judges a natural language demand as fulfilled.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does the skill convert token decimals?
faq.answer: No. It expects the amount in the token smallest unit, so users must calculate the value before execution.

faq.question: Can escrow terms include private information?
faq.answer: No. Demand text, provider, model, and prompt settings can be encoded on-chain and visible to others.

faq.question: What networks are documented?
faq.answer: The skill documents anvil, sepolia, base-sepolia, and mainnet, with a command to switch networks.

faq.question: What should I verify before creating an escrow?
faq.answer: Verify the wallet, network, token address, amount, oracle address, provider, model, prompt, and transaction consequences.
